questions.q: What is the parliamentary system of government, and how are the legislature and executive related?
answer: India follows a parliamentary system of government, in which the executive is drawn from the legislature and remains accountable to it.

answer.text: The government, or executive, must enjoy the confidence, that is the majority support, of the Lok Sabha to stay in power. If it loses that majority, it must resign.
The President is the constitutional or nominal head of the country, while the Prime Minister, who leads the majority party in the Lok Sabha, is the real head who exercises executive power.

The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, and the legislature controls the executive through debates, questions and the Budget. This keeps the government answerable to the people's representatives.

questions.q: Describe the Union Executive and the principle of separation of powers.

answer.text: The Union Executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers. The President is elected and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers. The Prime Minister leads the majority party in the Lok Sabha, and the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to it. The permanent executive, the civil services, actually implements government policies.

Power is divided among three organs — the legislature, which makes laws, the executive, which carries them out, and the judiciary, which interprets them. Each checks the others: the executive is answerable to the legislature, and the judiciary can review the actions of both, keeping a balance and preventing misuse of power.
